name: Bouregreg Marina
hero_subtitle: Modern marina and promenade on the Bouregreg — cafés, boats and views across to Salé.

overview.title: The capital’s new waterfront
overview.p1: The Bouregreg development links Rabat to a landscaped marina facing Salé. It is a different face of the capital: open promenades, cafés and evening strolls rather than Almohad stone. Useful after a day of monuments when you want a flat, easy walk.
overview.p2: Tram and taxi access are straightforward. Pair with a look at Salé or a sunset drink facing the water.

food.title: Eating at the marina
food.p1: Café and restaurant terraces along the marina. Quality varies — pick busy places.
food.p2: More refined tables remain in Hassan, Agdal and the medina.
food.li4: Return to L'Imprévu or medina for a special meal.
food.li5: Ice cream and snacks for families.

1.title: Access
1.desc: Taxi or tram toward the Bouregreg valley developments.

2.title: Wind
2.desc: Estuary breeze can be strong — bring a layer.

3.title: Salé
3.desc: Consider crossing for a different medina atmosphere.

q1.question: Is it a historic site?
q1.answer: No — modern waterfront complementary to the monuments.

q2.question: Worth it on a short trip?
q2.answer: Optional; prioritise Udayas, Hassan and Chellah first.

q3.question: Good for families?
q3.answer: Yes — flat walking and open space.

q4.question: Boat trips?
q4.answer: Seasonal offers may run on the river — ask locally.

q5.question: Nightlife?
q5.answer: Cafés and restaurants; not a club district.
